summary: FSM's ecosystem pledges focus primarily on marine and terrestrial conservation. The country committed to effectively managing 50% of its marine resources and 30% of its terrestrial resources by 2035, aligning with the expanded Micronesia Challenge 2030 (MC2030). Additionally, FSM pledged to restore, manage, and protect over 50% of coastal marine habitats—including coral reefs, seagrass, and wetlands—by 2035 to sustain nearshore fisheries. Commercial fishing will be restricted in up to 30% of the marine environment, and marine governance and surveillance systems will be strengthened across 30% of marine waters. The Blue Prosperity Micronesia program aims to protect 30% of FSM's ocean by 2030. The original Micronesia Challenge (2006) set earlier targets of conserving 30% of near-shore marine resources and 20% of terrestrial resources by 2020.

targets.context: ≈ 30% of the country's total land area (622 km²)

targets.metric: Marine waters with strengthened governance and surveillance
Coastal marine habitats restored, managed, and protected
